transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-09-07 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Recordings: enabled
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Redwood Solutions Eng); Anita Verma (Vellichor CISO), Liam O'Neal (Head of ML Ops), Sofia Ruiz (Legal), Jae Park (Platform)
Shared links: security pack (internal): https://redwood.example/security/pack/vellichor, KMS diagram: https://redwood.example/diagrams/kms-arch, sample SSO flow (pdf)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll try to keep this tight, high-level plus open Q&A. we got the agenda — SOC 2/ISO certs, RBAC/SSO patterns, audit logs, KMS/encryption, and then the specific ask: training opt-out and prompt retention.
[00:22] Anita (Vellichor): thanks, Maya. we just want to confirm upfront: we cannot have customer prompts used for training models. that's a hard req from legal and compliance.
[00:31] Diego (Redwood SE): yep totally understood. short answer: Redwood does not train upstream models on customer traffic for hosted workloads by default, and we offer a no-train contract clause for enterprise plans. there are also private/dedicated options where data never leaves customer VPCs.
[00:48] Liam (Vellichor): can you elaborate on both — hosted no-train and private? especially around telemetry, logs, and any side-channels like kv-cache?
[00:59] Diego: sure. hosted — we run inference in our shared control plane but with tenant isolation at the request layer, and we can opt you out of retention used for any model improvement. we still keep operational logs for billing and security but those are WORM-limited and can be configured for shorter retention. note: KV cache is for performance; we evict per policy and do not persist it beyond inference lifetime in no-train mode. (small laugh) sometimes auto-transcription calls it KV "cake" which is fun.
[01:32] Sofia (Legal): when you say "do not persist" — is that technical enforcement or policy? e.g., can we get an attestation?
[01:39] Maya: both. policy plus technical guardrails. we provide attestation language in the enterprise agreement and can include an appendix that lists which internal services touch data. we also provide logs showing retention TTLs and who accessed them.
[01:52] Jae (Platform): what about SSO and RBAC — we need SCIM sync, group-based RBAC, and time-limited admin sessions.
[02:01] Ravi (Redwood): we integrate with SAML/OKTA and OIDC. SCIM provisioning supported. RBAC supports role templates and custom roles; we also have audit trails for admin actions and token issuance. admin sessions can be limited, and we log session start/end and token refresh events.
[02:18] Anita: audit log granularity — do we get per-request metadata (IP, model variant, token cost) or just high-level summaries? we need per-request for investigations.
[02:28] Diego: we can export per-request JSON that includes timestamp, request id, model id, prompt hash, approximate token counts, latency, region, and whether the no-train flag was set. sensitive fields can be redacted at export time. the prompt hash allows correlation without keeping full prompt content if you prefer.
[02:53] Liam: prompt hash — is that reversible? we cannot have any reversible mapping to original PII.
[02:59] Diego: prompt hashes are one-way using salted HMAC; salt managed by your tenant KMS in private deployments, or by Redwood-managed KMS for hosted. for extra assurance we can return only partial hashes or do k-anonymity grouping.
[03:18] Sofia: about KMS — does Redwood support customer-managed keys (BYOK) and HSM-backed keys?
[03:24] Maya: yes. Dedicated and Private support customer-managed KMS via Cloud KMS or external HSM integrations; keys can be rotated and we record key rotations in audit logs. For hosted, we offer managed KMS but you can request BYOK on enterprise agreements.
[03:39] Jae: any certifications for key handling?
[03:42] Ravi: our KMS integrations meet cloud provider key-management best practices; we surface those details in the security pack — also our SOC 2 report covers key management controls.
[03:51] Anita: SOC 2 Type II — we need the latest report and an ISO 27001 cert if available.
[03:56] Maya: we'll send both. our SOC 2 Type II is current (2027-06 report) and we have ISO 27001 scoped to the inference platform; both will go out after the call.
[04:05] [04:05] — brief static pause while links exchanged —
[04:18] Liam: moving to data residency — we process in-region for EU and US customers; can you commit to EU-only processing for EU data?
[04:26] Diego: yes, with Dedicated or Private you can restrict to specific regions and we can pin capacity in a region. For hosted, we have region routing policies and can set a contractual clause for EU-only processing.
[04:39] Anita: what about backups and snapshots — are model caches or prompt logs ever included in backups stored outside region?
[04:45] Ravi: backups are regional by default. snapshots of infra are redacted and exclude prompt content for no-train customers; config snapshots may include metadata only.
[04:56] Sofia: okay on encryption at rest and in transit? TLS 1.2+ and AES-256?
[05:02] Maya: yes TLS 1.2/1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest. keys derive from KMS. we also support FIPS-compliant endpoints on request.
[05:12] Anita: on the 'no training' clause — can we have explicit language that our prompts and completions will never be used to update model weights, embeddings, or be included in training corpora?
[05:22] Diego: yes — the clause can be explicit. operationally we ensure that data marked no-train is excluded from any data pipelines that feed retraining or continuous improvement processes. the default open-source model variants we sometimes host are immutable and replaced by explicit model onboarding cycles, not customer data-driven updates.
[05:44] Liam: how do you prove that? can we run an annual compliance review or get a snapshot of pipeline configs?
[05:50] Maya: we provide pipeline manifests and a change log; for enterprise customers we also offer attestation and the ability to run a jointly agreed audit.
[05:59] Anita: PII/PHI — ours may include patient identifiers. do you offer automatic PII redaction or do we need to do that client-side?
[06:08] Diego: we have options: client-side redaction is recommended for max safety; Redwood offers built-in redaction rules and pre-processing hooks you can enable to mask fields (ssn, nhs id, dob). we also provide an opt-in PII scrubbing runtime that redacts before sending to any model. important caveat: scrubbing can affect model quality.
[06:32] Sofia: does scrubbing happen on-prem or in Redwood's control plane?
[06:36] Ravi: scrubbing can be run either client-side (recommended) or as a pre-processing step in a private deployment. in hosted mode, the scrubbing pipeline runs in our service but we can configure it under a no-train tenant so it never leaves the ephemeral boundary.
[06:53] [06:53] Anita: audit log retention — we need 7 years for certain logs. is that supported?
[06:59] Maya: we can retain audit logs for custom durations, 7 years supported as an add-on. access controls and immutable retention windows are configurable.
[07:10] Liam: a specific worry: does the auto-logging include full prompt text or only metadata? we want metadata only by default and full prompts kept only if explicitly requested and encrypted under customer KMS.
[07:22] Diego: default export and logs will be metadata-only (prompt hash, token counts); full prompt capture is opt-in and stored encrypted with customer-managed keys if requested.
[07:34] Jae: can you show a sample per-request log?
[07:38] Diego: yeah — share an example: {"ts":"2027-09-07T15:58:32Z","req_id":"r-abc123","model":"redwood-alpha-4k","region":"us-east-1","prompt_hash":"hmac-...","tokens":412,"latency_ms":142}. note: transcript sometimes mangles quotes and braces here in auto-export.
[08:00] Anita: about access controls — who at Redwood can read full prompts if we enable them?
[08:05] Maya: access is restricted to a named set of engineers under least-privilege. we can provide a matrix listing job-roles with access, and RBAC entries for your tenant; all access events are logged and surfaced in the audit trail.
[08:19] Sofia: can we have legal rights to request deletion or on-demand scrubbing?
[08:24] Maya: yes — our deletion API supports on-demand deletion of retained prompt content and we keep deletion audit logs. for hosted customers under no-train, deletion is usually automatic per TTL but you can trigger immediate purge.
[08:36] Liam: performance tradeoffs — if we force client-side redaction and short TTLs, what latency/cost changes do we expect?
[08:43] Diego: client-side redaction adds negligible latency (ms) but short TTLs reduce cache hit rate so token costs may go up 8–20% depending on workload. we can model this against your sample workloads once you share prompt distributions.
[09:03] [09:03] — short back-and-forth on pricing impact —
[09:08] Anita: legal wants explicit indemnity language in case of data leakage due to Redwood negligence; is that in standard enterprise agreement?
[09:15] Maya: yes indemnity in the EA covers Redwood negligence; specific caps and wording negotiable. we'll loop in legal after the packet is shared.
[09:23] Sofia: one more: telemetry for debugging — stacktraces, memory dumps — do those ever include prompt fragments?
[09:29] Ravi: no — telemetry is scrubbed. debug traces include request ids and non-sensitive metadata; any dump containing prompt text is restricted and requires explicit elevated access and logging.
[09:40] Liam: can we do a short pilot in our staging where we keep everything in our VPC and connect Redwood control plane for billing only?
[09:47] Maya: yes that's a common pattern: private runtime (in VPC) + Redwood control plane for management, with zero access to raw prompts from Redwood. we have docs for that topology.
[09:56] Anita: about monitoring and SLOs — we need 99.9 latency p95 for inference with 2k token workloads. can you commit?
[10:04] Diego: SLA is configurable — Dedicated can meet that SLO; hosted depends on model variant and burst policy. we can run a benchmark with your 2k workload and measure p95 under 99.9 target.
[10:16] [10:16] — discussion about model variants vs quantized versions —
[10:28] Maya: quick recap: we'll send SOC 2 and ISO certs, KMS architecture and BYOK options, sample per-request log format, an attestation template for no-train, and a pilot layout doc for private VPC runtime.
[10:42] Anita: and we'll send sample prompts and PHI field list. once legal reviews attestation we'll finalize.
[10:48] Maya: perfect. any final Qs?
[10:52] Liam: none from me. thanks.
[10:54] Sofia: thanks everyone.
[10:56] Maya: thanks — we'll follow up with the packet. bye.

Meeting close.

Notes about transcription: occasional word swaps (KV cake / KV cache), some speaker labels simplified by auto-transcription, timestamps are approximate.
